# ui::TrayIconOptions

Header: `winui/ui/TrayIcon.hpp`.

What a [TrayIcon](tray-icon.md) is created with: the icon, its hover text, its right-click menu and, optionally, the window a click opens next to it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> quiet{false};

ui::TrayIcon tray{{
    .tool_tip = ui::bind(quiet, [](bool q) { return std::string{q ? "Timer (muted)" : "Timer"}; }),
    .icon     = ui::WindowIcon{.glyph = ui::IconGlyph{0xE916}},
    .menu     = {{.text = "Quit", .on_click = [] { ui::quit(); }}},
}};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_tip` | `Binding<std::string>` |  | The icon's hover text. The shell cuts it at 127 characters. |
| `icon` | `Binding<WindowIcon>` |  | The icon, drawn at the taskbar's small-icon size. [`ui::WindowIcon{.resource = "#101"}`](window-icon.md) uses the executable's own icon resource. Empty shows the stock application icon. |
| `icon_follows_taskbar_theme` | `bool` | `true` | A glyph icon on a transparent background is drawn black on a light taskbar and white on a dark one, whatever `icon.foreground` says, and redrawn when the user switches. Without it, a white glyph is invisible on a light taskbar. |
| `menu` | `std::vector<MenuItem>` |  | The right-click menu, top to bottom. It uses each item's text, `on_click`, `command` and `enabled`, separators, and the `checked` state of toggle and radio items. A toggle flips and a radio item unchecks its group as in any menu, and `.checked = prop` follows and writes the property. The app writes every item, including its way out (`{.text = "Quit", .on_click = [] { ui::quit(); }}`). Change it later with set_menu(). |
| `flyout` | `Window*` | `nullptr` | A window the app owns, opened next to the icon by a click and hidden by the next one. Create it with [tray_flyout_options()](namespace-ui.md#tray_flyout_options). It must outlive the [TrayIcon](tray-icon.md). With nullptr the icon has no flyout, and a click runs `on_click`. |
| `flyout_max_height` | `float` | `0.0f` | The flyout is as tall as its content, measured each time it opens, up to this many DIPs. Zero makes it as tall as the work area allows, less the margin. |
| `flyout_margin` | `float` | `12.0f` | Space between the flyout and the taskbar, and the screen edges beside it, in DIPs. |
| `light_dismiss` | `bool` | `true` | Close the flyout when it stops being the active window, such as on a click anywhere else, Alt+Tab or the Win key. Otherwise it stays open until hide_flyout() or a second click on the icon. |
| `flyout_background` | `std::optional<Color>` |  | The flyout's fill. nullopt uses the theme's flyout surface. |
| `on_click` | `Callback<void()>` |  | A click or Enter on the icon, when there is no `flyout`. |
| `on_notification_click` | `Callback<void()>` |  | The user clicked the last notification, when it had no `on_click` of its own. Empty opens the flyout. |
